description_top: Replaying recorded logs against a new build sounds like a batch job. It is only worth running if the same inputs give the same answer, and a release gate is only worth having if it can fail for the right reason. A compact reference solution at the Staff bar (L6/L7): theory, a three-version design, an alternate path, and six challenges. {DURATION} minutes, {SLIDES} numbered slides.
The thesis: make every run a pure function of a pinned manifest, so outputs can be cached by content and differences mean something; then gate on paired statistics under a versioned policy.

IN THIS VIDEO
• Estimates: 250 TB and about 1,040 GPUs for an uncached 50,000-scenario gate, about $1 M a month of compute, 100 TB of cache
• Theory: six places randomness hides, five mechanisms (pinned manifests, simulated time, Merkle stage keys, paired intervals, quotas)
• Six challenges: the same build giving two answers, a perception change, release day, a log that does not react, block or pass, and a gate that cannot fail

HOW TO USE IT
Run the round cold first. Then watch once straight through. On the second pass, pause after each interviewer question and answer it first.

post: "Set the random seed" fixes one of the six ways a replay gives two answers. The grade is on the other five.
I've published a {DURATION}-minute reference solution for a log-replay and regression-gate platform at the Staff bar: theory, a three-version design and six challenges, on {SLIDES} numbered slides.

The idea that unlocks it: make every run a pure function of a pinned manifest. Then outputs can be cached by the hash of everything that made them, a difference between two builds means the build changed, and the gate can compare pairs instead of guessing at noise.

What it goes into:
→ Message ordering, GPU atomics and the wall clock
→ Merkle keys: what a perception change must recompute
→ Release day against 3,000 engineers
→ A gate that must prove it can fail
Best on a second pass: pause after each question and answer it first.
It's a scripted walkthrough with synthetic voices, built with Claude Code from design-room, my open-source system design interview simulator.
How do you know your own regression gate can still fail?
